newsitem.title: HUNGARY: NATO-Russia deal will not affect new members-Hungary.
newsitem.headline: NATO-Russia deal will not affect new members-Hungary.

text.p: Hungary said it was sure NATO had not made concessions affecting potential new members in its agreement reached on Wednesday with Russia on a new security relationship.

"We dont know the text of the agreement...but I have no reason to believe NATO has given any concession which would create diffulties for the countries which want to join NATO," Hungarian Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs told Reuters on Wednesday.

The agreement was reached between NATO Secretary General Javier Solana and Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov on the second day of the latest talks intended to placate Russia before NATO invites new members from eastern Europe.

Hungary, along with Poland and the Czech Republic are expected to receive the first invitations to join NATO at the alliance's July summit in Madrid, though Romania and Slovenia also hope to be in the first wave.

Wednesday's accord cleared the way for President Boris Yeltsin and NATO to sign a final deal on a new peaceful relationship in Paris on May 27, providing the text is approved by the Kremlin leader and the heads of government of the 16 NATO countries.
Details of the agreement were not immediately released and it was not clear if all differences had been fully resolved.

A breakthrough had been blocked until now by disagreements over whether the pact should include written guarantees that NATO will not station military structures and nuclear weapons on the territory of new member states.
Kovacs said he believed NATO had not changed its position against formal guarantees on nuclear weapons.
"I don't think, having in mind the earlier unilateral declaration that NATO doesn't see any reason to change the current posture of nuclear weapons, that there is now a formal agreement," he said.

Kovacs added that with or without a NATO-Russia accord he expected that first group of new members would be invited to join NATO in Madrid but welcomed the deal as a means of decreasing international tension surrounding NATO expansion.

"I don't think there is a direct relationship between the the agreement (between NATO and Russia) and the enlargement of NATO but certainly it would create a better atmosphere for enlargement," he said.
